ideas.premise: Every night at 3:12 my doorbell camera records someone standing on my porch, facing away. Tonight the notification came while I was standing on the porch.
ideas.twist: The figure in the recording is me, and the recordings are from tomorrow.
ideas.why_chapters: Each night's recording shows the figure closer to the door, giving five escalating chapters.

ideas.premise: The apartment elevator in my building has a button for a floor that does not exist. Last week it lit up by itself and the doors opened.
ideas.twist: The extra floor is a copy of my own apartment, with the lights already on.
ideas.protagonist: a delivery driver who rents the top-floor unit

ideas.premise: My grandmother's sewing machine starts on its own whenever someone in the house is about to lie. It stitched a single word into a hem this morning.
ideas.twist: The word is my name, and the hem belongs to the dress I am buried in.
ideas.protagonist: a college student home for the holidays

ideas.premise: The night janitor at a small library keeps finding one book left open on the same table. Each night the open page is closer to the end.
ideas.twist: The book is the janitor's own life, and the last page is tonight.
ideas.setting: a small town library after closing
ideas.protagonist: a retired teacher working nights as a janitor

ideas.premise: A lifeguard counts swimmers every hour and always gets the same number. Today the count is one higher, and nobody can say who the extra swimmer is.
ideas.twist: The extra swimmer has been in the pool every day for years, and only she can see it.
ideas.protagonist: a teenage lifeguard on her first summer job

ideas.premise: The bus that stops outside my window at midnight is always empty and always has its lights on. Tonight the driver waved at me.
ideas.twist: The route number on the bus is my apartment number, and the stop is my front door.

ideas.premise: A baby monitor in my new house picks up a lullaby every night at two. We have no baby.
ideas.twist: The previous owners left the monitor on purpose, and the lullaby is a warning meant for whoever lives in the nursery.
ideas.protagonist: a couple who just moved in

ideas.premise: Every morning my neighbor's porch light turns on at the exact minute my alarm goes off. Today I checked, and my alarm was set for a different time.
ideas.twist: My neighbor has been changing my alarm for months so that I am awake when something walks past.
ideas.protagonist: a bakery worker who wakes before sunrise
